summary: Request: Cross-region pseudonymized SIEM export with per-batch duplicate-detection manifest & legal evidence for payment-provider onboarding
description:
Issue summary:
Aurora Payments needs a production-ready SIEM export that: pseudonymizes user identifiers per-region, packages events into a cross-region envelope (single sequence across regions), and provides a per-batch duplicate-detection manifest (HMAC-based) and signed legal attestation for onboarding with their payments regulator.

Impact:
- Compliance blocking: Aurora cannot complete onboarding until they receive attested evidence that exported events are de-duplicable, pseudonymized deterministically per-tenant, and include tamper-evident manifests.
- Business: Aurora is awaiting a go/no-go for a production cutover scheduled next week.

Environment:
- Redwood prod clusters serving Aurora tenant (tenant-id: aurora-prod-10).
- Exports to Aurora SFTP endpoint us-east-1 and eu-west-1, currently set to per-region delta batches.

Requested deliverables (customer asks):
1) A cross-region envelope format spec that guarantees ordering (monotonic watermark) across regions for a given tenant for the export window.
2) Deterministic reversible pseudonymization spec (per-tenant salt) and sample output demonstrating pseudonymization applied.
3) Per-batch duplicate-detection manifest (per-file HMAC + sequence range + record-count + sample hash) and approach for resumable replays.
4) Signed legal attestation (short form) that the export mechanism preserves order and includes tamper-evident manifests suitable for regulator review.
5) Implementation timeline and any migration steps required for Aurora to switch to the new export.

Steps to reproduce (current state):
1) Aurora consumes per-region SFTP batches from us-east and eu-west.
2) They run an ingest pipeline which occasionally detects duplicates when cross-region replication results in overlapping event windows (they provided a sample of three duplicate event UUIDs).
3) Aurora requests a single canonical export envelope so they can ingest once and avoid cross-region dupes.

Logs/attachments provided by customer:
- three-sample-duplicates.csv (attached)
- sftp-manifest-sample-us-east.json (attached)
- sftp-manifest-sample-eu-west.json (attached)
- onboarding-questionnaire.pdf (legal/regulatory checklist)

Acceptance criteria from Aurora:
- Spec doc describing envelope and per-batch manifest format (JSON schema).
- Working sample export (one-hour slice) with pseudonymization applied and batch manifests that validate with HMAC key provided to Aurora.
comments: 2026-03-10 | Aisha Patel (Support): Created ticket after intake call with Aurora. Customer provided sample duplicates and legal checklist. Asking for spec + sample export and short attestation text. Assigned to Diego for SRE/exports analysis.

2026-03-10 | Diego Morales (SRE): Confirmed receipt of samples. Initial hypothesis: duplicates are produced by per-region delta windows overlapping during cross-region DR replication. Need to review the export scheduler and file manifest generation code. Will pull recent export runs from S3 and check sequence watermarks. ETA initial findings by 2026-03-11 EOD.

2026-03-11 | Diego Morales (SRE): Investigation update: found that per-region exporters independently seed HWM (high-watermark) from local ingestion timestamps; small clock skew + retry semantics can create overlapping ranges. Also observed manifests currently contain only file-level checksums, not record-level counts and no HMAC. Attaching S3 prefixes: s3://redwood-exports/aurora-prod-10/us-east/2026-03-09/ and s3://redwood-exports/aurora-prod-10/eu-west/2026-03-09/.

2026-03-11 | Maya Kapoor (Eng, export-format): Proposed immediate mitigation: add per-file sequence-range (min_seq, max_seq) and record_count to manifests and include a manifest-level HMAC using per-tenant export key. For canonical cross-region envelope, propose a top-level envelope that lists ordered file fragments and an envelope HMAC. Will prototype PR for manifest schema and HMAC library.

2026-03-12 | Evan Ross (Legal/Compliance): Reviewed customer's onboarding checklist. We should not provide a formal legal opinion; however, we can provide an attestation template signed by the Redwood compliance team confirming the export format and tamper-evident guarantees given the HMACs and manifest model. Legal needs Confluence spec and sample export to generate attestation language.

2026-03-12 | Aurora (customer contact: Hannah Li): Thanks for fast triage. For pseudonymization we require deterministic per-tenant reversible pseudonymization using a tenant KEK; Aurora will provide public key for encrypting mapping manifests. Also request that HMAC keys be rotated monthly and that rotation metadata be included in manifests.
investigation_notes: Checked export-service logs for aurora-prod-10 between 2026-03-09T00:00Z and 2026-03-10T00:00Z. Found overlapping sequence ranges across regions where sequence numbers were derived from ingestion timestamps rather than global monotonic counters.

Hypothesis 1: Clock skew + per-region independent watermarking yields overlapping seq ranges -> duplicates at consumer. Mitigation: move to global monotonic sequence generator or include per-record digest + idempotency keys in manifest.

Hypothesis 2: Retries at exporter can produce duplicate files with same timestamp but different content; manifests currently do not include record_count or sequence ranges so consumer cannot de-duplicate deterministically. Mitigation: include (min_seq,max_seq,record_count,file_checksum,manifest_hmac).

Security considerations: Pseudonymization must be reversible only by Aurora (they requested KEK to wrap per-batch key). Support will not ship any plaintext mappings in the export. We'll provide sample mapping format encrypted with customer's public key or wrapped by their KMS.
resolution_notes:
Planned deliverables and timeline agreed with Aurora on 2026-03-12 call:
- 2026-03-14: Draft confluence spec for cross-region envelope and manifest schema (Maya).
- 2026-03-17: Prototype export sample (one-hour slice) with pseudonymization and manifest HMACs to Aurora SFTP test endpoints (Diego).
- 2026-03-19: Compliance attestation template completed by Legal (Evan) once sample delivered.
- Post-delivery: follow-up runbook for key rotation and migration steps.

Interim workaround provided to Aurora:
- We recommended Aurora enable idempotent ingest where their pipeline ignores records with identical record_id and sequence number and to block dual ingestion across regions until sample runs are validated. This reduces duplication risk for the cutover window.

Open action items:
- ENG: implement manifest schema changes + HMAC library and prototype (owner: Maya Kapoor).
- SRE: run one-hour production slice export to staging SFTP for Aurora and validate manifests (owner: Diego Morales).
- Legal: draft attestation once sample is validated (owner: Evan Ross).
- Customer: supply public key or KMS wrap info for mapping encryption and confirm test SFTP credentials (owner: Aurora).
